title: finding(app-shell): FieldStub slices the picklist preview BEFORE filtering, so a well-formed option behind malformed ones never renders and the +N counter overcounts
body:
Found while implementing objectui#8632 (the field inspector's malformed-option repair). Filed separately: that card is scoped to `ObjectFieldInspector` as the READER, and this is a second surface on the same screen — the field cards of the designer's form canvas.

## The defect

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/FieldStub.tsx`, `PicklistStub()`:

```ts
const opts = options ?? [];
const visible = opts.slice(0, single ? 1 : 3).filter((o) => o.value || o.label);
```

The slice happens BEFORE the filter. So entries the filter drops still consume the display budget, and a well-formed option sitting behind them is never rendered — while the overflow counter, computed as `opts.length - visible.length`, counts them all and reports a number no badge accounts for.

The entries that get dropped are exactly the ones `ObjectFormCanvas` produces for a malformed authored option: its own projection is `value: String(o.value ?? '')` with a non-string `label` mapped to undefined, so a bare string, a `null`, a number or an option with no `value` all arrive as `{ value: '', label: undefined }`.

## Measured

Driven directly against `FieldStub` with the projection `ObjectFormCanvas` hands it for the authored list `['draft', 'open', 'closed', { value: 'real', label: 'Real' }]` — three malformed entries followed by one well-formed one:

```
multiselect card ->  "Pick one or more…+4"
select card      ->  "Select…"
```

The multiselect card shows the empty-state placeholder AND a `+4` counter, with zero badges. The select card reads as a field with no options at all. In both, the one option that IS well formed — `Real` — is not on screen. Swapping the order (well-formed entry first) renders it, which is what identifies the slice/filter ordering as the cause rather than the filter itself.

## Why this is filed rather than folded into objectui#8632

That card's ruling is scoped to the reader that WRITES — its severity is the silent deletion on commit, and its repair is a strict `readOptions` plus an inline report on the row. This canvas is a read-only preview stub: it destroys nothing and it now sits next to an inspector that reports the same malformed option loudly, so the severity here is low. But it is a reproducible defect on its own terms — a well-formed option that the author authored, hidden from the surface that previews their form, with a counter that says something is there — and the ordering bug is mechanical and one line.

## Scope note

Two candidate repairs, not chosen here: filter then slice (renders `Real`, and the counter then means what it says), or keep the ordering and count only what the filter admits. Which one is right depends on whether the canvas should show a malformed option AT ALL now that the inspector reports it — a product question this card does not answer.

Not to be confused with objectui#8632, which is the inspector, and with objectui#8488, which is a stored value matching no option in `InspectorSelectField`.

Filed by the objectui#8632 execution seat, session `session_01MPaVWWMuWeT5LgB1qoXjVB`. No assignee and no labels on purpose — grading and routing belong to triage.
